answer: A memory-hard sequential proof of work is bound to a non-transferable tenure record, so the work cannot be parallelised across clones, cannot be sold to another identity, and cannot be reused, because the memory-hardness forces one sequential chain per identity. Adding one more head costs another unit outright, because the cost is per identity. The ripple is the sequential proof, the vault the tenure it is bound to, and the bridge the memory-hardness that resists parallel evaluation; the ripple and the vault are per identity, and it is the bridge that stops one proof serving a hundred clones.
